name: gh-api-is-not-a-bypass
description:
Per-subcommand permissions are worth only as much as the weakest route to the same effect. `gh pr create` was external#github_repo_url#write while `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/pulls` opened the same pull request as passthrough — no check, no approval, no record. Found by running it: asked to summarise a repository, a live agent used `gh api` twice and finished with ZERO permissioned calls.

Two calls, because the fix has two halves and one call can only show one. A repo-scoped GET resolves to readonly#read and is ALLOWED by the fixture's grant — `gh pr view` reads the same object, and routing an identical read through a human was over-restriction, not security. A POST to the same endpoint falls through to the external#write fallback and is refused.

Both assertions are mutation-sensitive in different directions. Revert the toolkit to passthrough and NEITHER decision is recorded at all (a passthrough Permission carries no Check, so recordAuthzDecision returns early). Delete the GET variant and the read is charged write, so the #read key disappears.
